column1: # scripts/verify/mutants.tsv - the mutant catalogue
# One row per mutant: the source change that reintroduces the defect a test
# claims to cover. `tests.tsv` selects a mutant by name (`red = mutant:<name>`);
# this file says what that name does. Nothing here is executed: the engine is
# riscv_mutant_apply() in common.cmake, and it treats the file as text -- it
# knows nothing about SystemVerilog.
#   name <TAB> file <TAB> find <TAB> replace <TAB> why
# name      the string tests.tsv names as `mutant:<name>`
# file      path relative to the repository root
# find      the exact text to replace; it must occur EXACTLY once in file,
#           otherwise the mutant is stale and the gate aborts
# replace   the text that reintroduces the defect
# why       one line, printed when the mutant is applied and by --list
# '#' starts a comment line; a comment block above a row is that mutant's
# rationale. `;` is escaped by riscv_tsv_rows()/riscv_tsv_cell(), so SV
# statements with a semicolon are fine in a cell. The root-cause narrative
# stays in doc/verification.md (G-20/G-26/G-27, FR-12); this file only says
# what the mutation does.
# T-06 (FR-12): the pre-fix core ignored the address low bits and always
# extended the byte at the highest address, so 8 of the 12 T-06 cases stored
# the wrong value. Pinning the lane to 3 reproduces exactly that.

column4: assign ld_lane = 2'b11; // negative control: lane never selected
column5: the sub-word lane is not selected from the address (pre-fix FR-12)

column1: # T-08 (NFR-05): rv32ui-p-simple has no test case; the verdict rests on ADDI
# producing 1 and the store reaching tohost. Ignoring the second operand turns
# `li gp,1` into `li gp,0` and breaks `la t5,tohost`, so the harness must
# report SANITY: TIMEOUT plus a UVM error.
sanity-addi
column4: alu_result = alu_data1.s_data; // negative control: ADD ignores the second operand
column5: ADDI/ADD ignore their second operand, so `li gp,1` writes 0 and the pass store writes 0

column1: # T-09 (WP-4b): T-09 sets is_active=UVM_PASSIVE and requires the monitor only.
# Removing the guard builds the driver/sequencer in passive mode.
passive-agent-always-active
column4: if (1'b1) begin // negative control: UVM_PASSIVE ignored
column5: the agent builds the driver/sequencer even when is_active=UVM_PASSIVE

column1: # T-10 (G-27): reverting pc_id to the current `pc` misaligns the decoder PC by
# one instruction: a branch at 0xa0 targets 0x53c instead of 0x538.
branch-redirect
column4: pc_id <= pc; // negative control: one-instruction PC misalignment
column5: the decoder sees the next instruction's PC, so a branch target is +4 (G-27)

column1: # T-11 (G-26): alu_ex is the EX source of the ALU/jump forwarding; leaving it
# unknown loses the predecessor's value.
forward-rs1
column4: assign alu_ex = 'x; // negative control: EX forward source missing
column5: the EX-stage forward source is unknown, so the predecessor's value is lost (G-26)

column1: # T-12 (G-20): slicing imm[20:0] zero-extends a negative offset and sends the
# branch to the 0x200000-family; rv32ui-p-beq times out.
negative-branch
column4: jump_addr = base_addr + imm[20:0]; // negative control: zero-extended offset
column5: a negative branch/jump offset is zero-extended (G-20)

column1: # T-13 (FR-11 / G-08): rv32ui-p-sb walks every byte lane. Dropping the lane
# shift leaves the stored byte at lane 0 while the strobe selects the addressed
# byte, so every SB above lane 0 writes a zero.
store-lane-offset
column4: rs2_lane.u_data = rs2_pipeline.u_data; // negative control: byte store ignores the lane
column5: the byte value is not placed in the addressed lane (G-08)

column1: # T-14 (FR-11 / G-22): rv32ui-p-sh stores at offsets 0 and 2. A halfword
# strobe of 4'b1111 contradicts the halfword width and claims two bytes the
# store did not drive.
store-strb-all
column4: data_wr_strb_ex = 4'b1111; // negative control: halfword strobe drives all four bytes
column5: a halfword store announces four bytes (G-22)

column1: # T-15 (FR-11 / G-08, G-22): rv32ui-p-st_ld mixes byte, half and word. Forcing
# the width port to byte makes every halfword/word store report 2'b00 next to a
# 2- or 4-bit strobe, which the strb_checker rejects even when the image's own
# software verdict would pass.
store-width-cast
column4: assign data_rd_wr_ctrl = 2'b00; // negative control: width port forced to byte
column5: the width port reports byte for every access (FR-11, the old one-bit cast)

column1: # T-16 (FR-17 / G-30): rv32ui-p-ld_st branches at 0xa4 on `sp`, which the load
# at 0x9c has just written and is still in MA. The frozen branch re-evaluates
# correctly one cycle later, but the stale echo of the first decision is
# registered without the qualifier, so the fetch that follows the branch is
# flushed and the image loses the instruction at 0xa8. Reverting the redirect
# alone (`if (branch_taken)`) does NOT reproduce: with the echo still qualified
# the held branch recovers, so the mutant targets the registered echo.
branch-taken-stale
column4: branch_taken_q <= branch_taken; // negative control: stale branch echo
column5: a stale branch decision is echoed and flushes the fetch that follows the branch (G-30)

column1: # T-17 (FR-07 / G-31): rv32ui-p-jalr computes its target from a register the
# previous instruction produced. Closing the jump-forward mux to cond_jump
# leaves that rs1 stale, so every JALR after its producer jumps to the wrong
# place and the image never reaches tohost (the original G-31 timeout).
jalr-no-forward
column4: cond_jump)) begin // negative control: JALR rs1 not forwarded
column5: a JALR target reads a stale rs1 because the jump-forward mux is closed (G-31)

column1: # T-37 (FR-07): the local image jumps through an odd address. With the mask
# removed the target stays odd; the word-indexed image memory still returns the
# word at the aligned address, but the unaligned PC makes the test's PC-relative
# `la` compute linkaddr_3 + 1 and its `bne` sends the image to fail (testnum 3).
jalr-keep-bit0
column4: jump_addr = jump_addr; // negative control: JALR target keeps bit 0
column5: an odd JALR target is not masked to an instruction boundary (FR-07)

column1: # T-29..T-36 (FR-01): SUB, SLL, SLT, SLTU, XOR, SRL, SRA and OR read their
# second operand from rs2 (directly or through the EX/MA/WB forward muxes).
# Selecting the immediate side for every op makes each of them compute with 0
# instead of rs2; the I-type instructions used to build the test data (`li`,
# `la`) are unaffected, so the image reports the failing TESTNUM.
alu-ignore-rs2
column4: case (IMM_S2) // negative control: every ALU op reads the immediate side
column5: the ALU second operand ignores rs2, so the R-type instructions compute with the immediate

column1: # T-23..T-28 (FR-02/FR-03): SLTI, SLTIU, XORI, SRLI, SRAI and ANDI take their
# second operand from the immediate port. Zeroing that port makes the result
# independent of the encoded immediate, but it also breaks the PC-relative `la`
# that builds the tohost address, so these images reach the pass/fail ceremony
# with a wrong store address and the harness times out (SANITY: TIMEOUT,
# UVM_RESULT: FAIL) instead of storing a TESTNUM. The image fails either way.
imm-zero
column4: alu_data2 = '0; // negative control: immediate operand is zero
column5: the ALU immediate operand is zero, so the I-type instructions compute with 0

column1: # T-19..T-22 (FR-08): BLT, BGE, BLTU and BGEU are checked with both taken and
# not-taken cases. Forcing branch_taken for every conditional branch sends the
# not-taken cases (and every `bne ..., fail` guard) down the taken path, so the
# image stores a nonzero TESTNUM to tohost.
branch-always-taken
column4: if (cond_jump) branch_taken = 1'b1; else if (cond_jump) begin // negative control: every conditional branch taken
column5: every conditional branch is taken, so the not-taken cases reach `fail` (FR-08)

column1: # T-18 (FR-06): rv32ui-p-jal checks the link register and the branch target of
# JAL. Dropping the offset makes the jump target the instruction's own PC, so
# the core loops on the JAL forever and the harness never sees tohost.
jal-offset-zero
column4: jump_addr = base_addr; // negative control: jump target drops the offset
column5: JAL jumps to its own PC instead of PC+offset (FR-06)

column1: # T-38 reuses `branch-always-taken` above (FR-08): rv32ui-p-bne has both taken
# and not-taken cases, and every `bne ..., fail` guard is taken, so the image
# reports a nonzero TESTNUM.
# T-39 (FR-02): rv32ui-p-ori takes its function from the ALU_OR arm. The body
# line `alu_result = alu_data1 | alu_data2;` cannot be the `find` of a TSV row
# (a cell may not contain `|`, it is the table separator), so the same defect
# is introduced one line up: the case selector routes ALU_OR into the AND arm,
# and ORI computes AND. Test 2 expects 0xffffff0f and reads 0xff00ff00, so the
# image reaches `fail`; the ceremony's own `ori gp,gp,1` then stores 0x0, which
# the checker reports as SANITY: FAIL testnum=0.
alu-or-to-and
column4: case (alu_op == ALU_OR ? ALU_AND : alu_op) // negative control: OR computes AND
column5: ALU_OR is routed into the AND arm, so ORI writes the bitwise AND (FR-02)

column1: # T-40 (FR-03): rv32ui-p-slli checks SLLI at shifts 0, 1, 7, 14 and 31. Keeping
# data1 and dropping the shift matches only shift 0, so TESTNUM 3 reports.
shift-left-zero
column4: alu_result = alu_data1; // negative control: the left shift is dropped
column5: SLL/SLLI return the unshifted first operand (FR-03)

column1: # T-41 (FR-04): rv32ui-p-lui reads the upper immediate back (`lui ra,0xfffff;
# srai ra,1` == -2048). Sending the LUI arm to ALU_ADD does NOT reproduce it:
# the rs1 field of those U-type encodings selects x0/x31/a6, all still zero, so
# rd is still the immediate. Zeroing the shared U-type immediate does, and the
# image reports TESTNUM 3. The same row also reaches AUIPC, which has its own
# mutant below.
lui-ignores-imm
column4: imm.s_data = '0; // negative control: U-type immediate zero
column5: LUI ignores its upper immediate and writes 0 (FR-04)

column1: # T-42 (FR-05): the decoder sets `alu_src1 = PC;` for AUIPC, but that line
# occurs three times (AUIPC, JAL, JALR) and a `find` must be unique. The defect
# is the same one arm up: PC_S1 in ALU mux 1 returns rs1, so AUIPC adds rs1
# (== x0 in this image) instead of pc and the image reports TESTNUM 5. The
# JAL/JALR link values move too; each of those has its own mutant.
auipc-no-pc
column4: alu_data1 = rs1; // negative control: the pc is not added
column5: AUIPC adds rs1 instead of pc, so rd is the immediate alone (FR-05)
